items.title: Action required: decide how long anonymous sharing links should last
items.summary:
Microsoft is changing the default expiration for anonymous sharing links in SharePoint Online and OneDrive. Links created before the change keep working until their new expiration date unless an administrator sets a policy of their own.
How this will affect your organization: Anonymous links will stop working sooner than they do today when no policy is set.
What you need to do to prepare: Review the sharing settings in the SharePoint admin center, decide whether to keep the new default or set your own, and tell the teams that rely on long-lived links.

definition.title: Inactive accounts
definition.description: Every account and how long it has gone without signing in, from Microsoft's last sign-in dates. Pick a range or sort by days.

columns.label: Inactive for
columns.help: Days since the last successful sign-in. With no success on record, since the last attempt; with no sign-in at all, since the account was created.

columns.label: Last successful sign-in
columns.help: Interactive or background. Microsoft has recorded this since 1 December 2023.

columns.label: Last interactive attempt
columns.help: The last time the person signed in themselves, successfully or not.

columns.label: Last background attempt
columns.help: The last time an app signed in for the person, successfully or not.

columns.label: Domain
columns.help: The part of the sign-in name after the @. Filter by it to look at one domain without changing the audit scope.

requirements: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 in the tenant, which Microsoft requires for sign-in dates.
A role that can read sign-in activity, such as Reports Reader, Security Reader or Global Reader.

notes: Days count from the last successful sign-in, interactive or background. Microsoft has recorded successful sign-ins only since 1 December 2023, so an account with none since then is counted from its last attempt, which can only make it look more recent.
Attempts, no success: accounts that tried to sign in after December 2023 with no successful sign-in on record. Check them for a broken account or someone guessing passwords.
Never signed in means Microsoft has no sign-in on record. Its records start in April 2020, so these accounts are counted from creation or April 2020, whichever is later.
Shared mailboxes, rooms and equipment are accounts too and normally never sign in.

definition.title: Licenses to reclaim
definition.description: Licensed accounts that are disabled or have not signed in for 30 days or more, and how each license was assigned.

columns.label: Inactive for
columns.help: Counted the same way as the Inactive accounts audit. Empty when last sign-in dates could not be read.

columns.label: Assigned
columns.help: A license assigned by a group comes back if you remove it directly. Remove the account from the group instead.

columns.label: Domain
columns.help: The part of the sign-in name after the @. Filter by it to look at one domain without changing the audit scope.

requirements: Without sign-in dates (AuditLog.Read.All with Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2), only disabled accounts are listed.

notes: By product: Microsoft 365 Business Premium 11, Microsoft Power Automate Free 6, Exchange Online (Plan 1) 2.
Microsoft does not report prices, so Prism365 counts seats, not cost.

definition.title: MFA registration
definition.description: Who has registered a strong sign-in method and who has not, with the admins who rely on phone or text codes. From Microsoft's authentication methods report.

columns.label: MFA registered
columns.help: Microsoft's definition: at least one strong method your authentication methods policy allows is registered.

columns.label: Domain
columns.help: The part of the sign-in name after the @. Filter by it to look at one domain without changing the audit scope.

requirements: A role such as Reports Reader, Security Reader, Security Administrator or Global Reader.

notes: Microsoft's report leaves out disabled accounts.
Registered is not the same as required. Conditional Access or security defaults decide whether a sign-in asks for MFA.
Phone or text only: the strongest method registered is a text message or call, which phishing and SIM swaps can defeat. Move these accounts, admins first, to the Authenticator app or a passkey.
Microsoft refreshes this report on its own schedule. Report updated shows when each row was refreshed.

definition.title: Guest accounts
definition.description: External guests in the tenant: invitations never accepted, guests who never signed in, and guests who have gone quiet.

columns.label: Invited
columns.help: When the guest account was created, which is when the invitation was sent.

columns.label: Inactive for
columns.help: Counted the same way as the Inactive accounts audit. Empty when last sign-in dates could not be read.

requirements: Sign-in dates need AuditLog.Read.All and Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2. Without them, only invitation states are shown.

notes: Every guest here can sign in to whatever was shared with it until the account is disabled or removed.

definition.title: License capacity
definition.description: Each product the tenant subscribes to: seats bought, assigned and free, and subscriptions that have expired or been suspended.

columns.label: In grace period
columns.help: Seats on an expired subscription that can still be assigned until it is renewed or suspended.

columns.label: Available
columns.help: Active and grace-period seats not assigned to anyone. Negative means more are assigned than owned.

requirements: A role that can read subscriptions, such as Directory Readers, Global Reader or License Administrator.

notes: Needs attention: no seats left to assign, more assigned than owned, or a subscription that has expired, been suspended or been locked out.
Products with 10,000 seats or more are usually free or self-service sign-up products, so their seats are not counted as unassigned.
Microsoft does not report prices or renewal dates here, so Prism365 shows seats only.

definition.title: Conditional Access policies
definition.description: Every Conditional Access policy with who it applies to, who it leaves out and what it requires, and whether the tenant blocks legacy authentication and asks administrators for MFA.

columns.label: State
columns.help: On enforces the policy. Report only evaluates and logs it without enforcing it.

columns.label: Leaves out
columns.help: Users, groups and roles the policy skips. User names appear when the session has granted User.Read.All.

columns.label: Conditions
columns.help: Client apps, platforms, locations and risk levels the policy narrows to. Locations are named from the tenant's named locations.

columns.label: Grant
columns.help: What a sign-in must satisfy. With one of, any listed control is enough.

requirements: A role such as Global Reader, Security Reader, Security Administrator or Conditional Access Administrator.
Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.

summary.label: No enabled policy blocks legacy authentication

notes: Report-only policies are evaluated and logged but not enforced, so the checks above leave them out.

Blocks legacy authentication means an enabled policy for all users that blocks Exchange ActiveSync and other legacy clients. Requires MFA means the grant includes MFA or an authentication strength; when the operator is OR, another listed control can satisfy it instead. Neither check looks at apps, locations, risk levels or exclusions.

Security defaults are not Conditional Access policies and are not read here. When they are on, Microsoft blocks legacy authentication and requires MFA for administrators, so a missing policy above may not leave the tenant open.
Policies refer to roles by role template ID. Prism365 names the common administrator roles and counts the rest.
Users excluded from MFA policies often include break-glass (emergency access) accounts, which are excluded on purpose. Check that every other account on the list is meant to be there.

definition.title: Risky users
definition.description: Accounts Microsoft Entra ID Protection marks as at risk or compromised, with the risk level, why, and whether the risk has been dealt with.

columns.label: Risk level
columns.help: Microsoft's level for the account. Hidden means the account is not covered by ID Protection.

columns.label: Risk detail
columns.help: Why Microsoft last changed the risk, such as a password reset or an admin decision.

columns.label: Being processed
columns.help: Yes while Microsoft is still working out the user's risk, so the level may change.

columns.label: Domain
columns.help: The part of the sign-in name after the @. Filter by it to look at one domain without changing the audit scope.

requirements: Microsoft Entra ID P2.
A role such as Global Reader, Security Reader, Security Operator or Security Administrator.

summary.label: Remediated or dismissed in the last 30 days

notes: Microsoft keeps a risky user listed until the risk is remediated, so an old entry stays until someone closes it.
Hidden means the account is not covered by ID Protection, so Microsoft reports no risk for it.
These are Microsoft's detections. Prism365 adds none and judges nothing itself.

definition.title: Managed devices
definition.description: Devices enrolled in Intune: who has them, whether they pass compliance, when they last checked in, and which are personal, unencrypted or jailbroken.

columns.label: Compliance
columns.help: Intune's own verdict against the compliance policies assigned to the device. In grace period means the device has time to fix what failed.

columns.label: Last check-in
columns.help: When the device last contacted Intune. It says the device is reachable, not that anyone used it.

columns.label: Since check-in
columns.help: Days since the last check-in. Empty when Microsoft has no readable date.

columns.label: Jailbroken or rooted
columns.help: Microsoft reports this as True, False or Unknown. Unknown is common for devices Intune cannot inspect.

requirements: An active Intune license in the tenant, which Microsoft requires for its device API.
A role that can read Intune devices, such as Global Reader, Security Reader, Helpdesk Administrator or Intune Administrator, or the Read Only Operator role in Intune.

notes: The Ethernet MAC address is not shown. Microsoft returns it only when a device is read on its own, and this audit does not make a request per device.
Owner is the primary user Intune has on record. Shared and kiosk devices have none.
Encrypted and jailbroken are what the device reported to Intune. Unknown means it did not say, which is common for some platforms.

definition.title: App consents
definition.description: Every application that holds permissions in this tenant: what it can do without anyone signed in, what an administrator granted for all users, how many users consented for themselves, and which permissions are high-risk.

columns.label: Publisher
columns.help: The publisher Microsoft has verified for the app. Only apps owned by another organisation count as unverified: Microsoft's own apps and apps registered in this tenant do not.

columns.label: Owner
columns.help: Who registered the app: this tenant, Microsoft, or another organisation. Unknown when Microsoft gave no owner.

columns.label: High-risk permissions
columns.help: Permissions on Prism365's own short list: mail, files, chats, the directory and administrator roles. A prompt to review the app, not a verdict.

columns.label: Application permissions
columns.help: Granted to the app itself. It can use them with no one signed in.

columns.label: Delegated, all users
columns.help: Granted by an administrator for every user. The app uses them only while a person is using it. Not read without Directory.Read.All.

columns.label: Users who consented
columns.help: Users who agreed to the app's permissions for themselves, with no administrator involved.

requirements: A role that can read applications and their app role assignments, such as Directory Readers, Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator. Microsoft does not list Global Reader for reading app role assignments.
Delegated permissions (optional) need Directory.Read.All and a role such as Global Reader or Directory Readers.

summary.label: Apps with admin consent for everyone

notes: Microsoft's own apps are left out unless they hold permissions granted in this tenant.
Permissions granted or removed in the last few minutes may not show yet, because Microsoft's directory takes time to replicate.
Application permissions let an app act with no one signed in. Delegated permissions apply only while a person is using the app.

High-risk means the permission is on Prism365's short list: Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Read, Mail.Send, Mail.ReadBasic.All, Files.ReadWrite.All, Sites.ReadWrite.All, Directory.ReadWrite.All, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory, AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All, Application.ReadWrite.All, User.ReadWrite.All, full_access_as_app, EWS.AccessAsUser.All, Chat.Read.All. A prompt to review an app, not a verdict.
Unverified means Microsoft has not verified the app's publisher. Only apps owned by another organisation count: Microsoft's own apps and apps registered in this tenant do not.

definition.title: Microsoft 365 app usage
definition.description: Which accounts used Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote or Teams in the last 90 days, on which platforms, and which used none: reclaim candidates the license audits cannot see. For mail, Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint activity, see Account activity.

columns.label: Last activity
columns.help: The latest day the report shows the account using any of the six apps. Microsoft gives a date, not a time.

columns.label: Since activity
columns.help: Days since the last activity. Empty when the report has none in the period.

columns.label: Apps used
columns.help: Used at least once in the period.

columns.label: Platforms
columns.help: Where any of the apps was used in the period.

columns.label: Domain
columns.help: The part of the sign-in name after the @. Filter by it to look at one domain without changing the audit scope.

requirements: Reports Reader or a service administrator role (Exchange, SharePoint or Teams). Global Reader and Usage Summary Reports Reader see tenant totals only, not this per-user report.
Names show only when the tenant's report privacy setting shows them. A Global Administrator controls that setting.

summary.label: No Microsoft 365 app activity in 90 days

notes: Microsoft's usage reports lag by 24 to 72 hours and sometimes by several days, so the most recent activity can be missing.
The report covers the last 90 days and has columns for Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote and Teams only.
Per-user detail needs a role such as Reports Reader or a service administrator. Global Reader sees tenant totals only.

definition.title: Account activity
definition.description: Is this account really unused, and does anyone depend on it? One row per account: sign-ins, mail, Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint use, mailbox size, licenses and groups, with a verdict. The list to check before offboarding or reclaiming licenses.

columns.label: Verdict
columns.help: Active: signed in, or used mail, Teams, OneDrive or SharePoint, in the last 30 days. Signs in, uses nothing: signed in in the last 30 days, no use in 90. Quiet everywhere: no sign-in or use for 90 days. Quiet, others use their files: the same, yet its OneDrive shows file activity. Recently quiet: last seen 30 to 89 days ago. Never signed in: no sign-in on record, account over 30 days old. Not enough data: the reports or dates cannot settle it.

columns.label: Domain
columns.help: The part of the sign-in name after the @. Filter by it to look at one domain without changing the audit scope.

columns.label: Last successful sign-in
columns.help: Interactive or background. Microsoft has recorded this since 1 December 2023.

columns.label: Since sign-in
columns.help: Days since the last successful sign-in, counted as in the Inactive accounts audit: with no success on record, since the last attempt; with no sign-in at all, since the account was created.

columns.label: Last interactive attempt
columns.help: The last time the person signed in themselves, successfully or not.

columns.label: Last background attempt
columns.help: The last time an app signed in for the person, successfully or not.

columns.label: Mail last activity
columns.help: The later of the dates the active users report and the email report give. Microsoft gives a date, not a time. No data means the account has no row in the reports, or they were not read.

columns.label: Mail sent
columns.help: Messages sent in the last 90 days.

columns.label: Mail received
columns.help: Messages received in the last 90 days. Shown, but not counted as use of the account.

columns.label: Mail read
columns.help: Messages read in the last 90 days.

columns.label: Teams last activity
columns.help: The later of the dates the active users report and the Teams report give.

columns.label: Teams chats
columns.help: Team chat and private chat messages sent in the last 90 days.

columns.label: Teams calls
columns.help: Calls in the last 90 days.

columns.label: Teams meetings attended
columns.help: Meetings attended in the last 90 days.

columns.label: OneDrive last activity
columns.help: The later of the dates the active users report and the OneDrive activity report give: what the account's owner did.

columns.label: OneDrive files viewed or edited
columns.help: Files the account's owner viewed or edited in the last 90 days.

columns.label: OneDrive account last file activity
columns.help: From the OneDrive usage report, which describes the account's OneDrive rather than what its owner did. Microsoft does not say whose activity it counts.

columns.label: OneDrive active files
columns.help: Files in the account's OneDrive that were active in the last 90 days. Activity here on a quiet account means someone still opens its files; Microsoft does not say who.

columns.label: OneDrive files
columns.help: Files in the account's OneDrive.

columns.label: OneDrive storage used (GB)
columns.help: Gigabytes used. A gigabyte here is 1,073,741,824 bytes.

columns.label: SharePoint last activity
columns.help: The later of the dates the active users report and the SharePoint activity report give.

columns.label: SharePoint files viewed or edited
columns.help: Files viewed or edited in the last 90 days.

columns.label: SharePoint pages visited
columns.help: Pages visited in the last 90 days.

columns.label: Mailbox storage used (GB)
columns.help: Gigabytes used. A gigabyte here is 1,073,741,824 bytes.

columns.label: Mailbox items
columns.help: Items in the mailbox.

columns.label: Mailbox last activity
columns.help: From the mailbox usage report. It counts as use of the account.

columns.label: Mailbox has archive
columns.help: Some of Microsoft's reports leave this out.

columns.label: License assignment
columns.help: Direct, Through groups, Both or None. A license assigned through a group comes back if you remove it from the account: remove the account from the group instead.

columns.label: License groups
columns.help: The groups that assign a license the account holds.

columns.label: Groups
columns.help: Direct memberships only: nested groups are not followed. Directory roles and administrative units are counted apart.

columns.label: Directory roles
columns.help: Directory roles the account holds directly, such as Global Administrator.
